terms.comment: No reference work has a Latin word. Allergia is the international medical name, coined in 1906 from Greek ἄλλος, other, and ἔργον, work, and used in every European language; Latin speakers use it as it is.

terms.gloss: be bad for: be allergic to
terms.grammar: verb, second conjugation, with the dative
terms.comment: The everyday way to say it, with the thing as subject: nucēs eī nocent, nuts are bad for him.

phrases.english: He’s allergic to nuts; don’t give him any.

sources: Lewis & Short: noceo
